tagline: The tougher 1986 arcade remix of Super Mario Bros., preserved through Arcade Archives.
notFitFor: Players looking for a long campaign
Players who want online cooperative multiplayer

gameplayPillars.title: Arcade-authentic Mario
gameplayPillars.description: Play Nintendo's VS. System version rather than the standard NES home release.

gameplayPillars.title: Higher difficulty
gameplayPillars.description: Course layouts and item/enemy placement are tuned to a more demanding arcade experience.

gameplayPillars.title: Arcade Archives tools
gameplayPillars.description: Change difficulty and display options and compete on online high-score rankings.

worldSummary: The familiar Mushroom Kingdom appears in a more difficult arcade arrangement. VS. SUPER MARIO BROS. reuses the core structure of the original but changes enemy and item placement and incorporates more demanding course layouts.

storyChapters.title: World 1
storyChapters.body: The classic rescue begins with familiar Mushroom Kingdom imagery but arcade-specific placements.

storyChapters.title: Harder worlds
storyChapters.body: Later stages incorporate more difficult layouts and patterns.

storyChapters.title: Rescue Peach
storyChapters.body: Reach Bowser's final castle and complete the original arcade challenge.

perfResolutionDocked: Original arcade framebuffer presented through 1080p Switch output
perfResolutionHandheld: Original arcade framebuffer presented through 720p Switch output
perfNotes: The title emulates an 1986 arcade game; Nintendo does not publish a modern native rendering-resolution metric. Switch and Switch 2 compatibility preserve the game's original behavior with system-level output scaling.
storageNotes: Nintendo lists 98 MB on both Switch and Switch 2. microSD storage is unnecessary for most users.
languagesText: Additional regional English/French variants in Nintendo storefront

dlc.name: No paid DLC
dlc.description: This digital Arcade Archives release has no paid expansion.

dlc.name: Arcade Archives features included
dlc.description: Difficulty, display and ranking features are part of the base purchase.

dlc.name: No physical edition
dlc.description: Nintendo lists the title as a digital edition; therefore no genuine retail box/full-wrap texture exists.

faq.q: Is this the same as the NES Super Mario Bros.?
faq.a: No. It is the 1986 Nintendo VS. System arcade version with different enemy/item placement and harder layouts.
Yes. Nintendo marks it as supported with behavior consistent with Nintendo Switch.

verdictSummary: A historically interesting and well-preserved arcade variation of Super Mario Bros.; its main appeal is challenge, authenticity and score chasing rather than new content.
verdictPros: Small download and useful emulator options
Interesting harder layouts for Mario historians
verdictCons: No true retail box or physical edition
Less accessible than the normal NES version

reviews.quote: A tougher but enjoyable alternative to the home-console original.
Official listing confirms Switch 2 compatibility and 98 MB size.
Arcade Archives publisher page confirms the 1986 origin and 1–2 player support.
